phases.name: Slice-01 — Record who builds each scraped repo (US-CPI-001) + the thin walking-skeleton thread through slices 02/03

steps.name: Scraping a repo records its top-30 human contributors in an append-only local link table and names the excluded bots
steps.description: First vertebra of WS-CPI-1. (a) EXTEND GithubPort with a contributors read + raw contributor row + named ContributorsUnavailable variant (DDD-2); adapter-github issues ONE public GET /repos/{o}/{r}/contributors?per_page=100. (b) PURE selection in a new scraper-domain `people` area: bot rule, re-rank (contributions desc, login asc), de-dup by user id, top-N (default 30), bots_excluded (DDD-3). (c) NEW ContributionLinkPort (no delete/update) + migration v5 `contribution_links` (DDD-5) + DuckDbContributionLinkAdapter on the shared connection with a LIVE probe (upsert-twice sentinel in a rolled-back tx, DDD-15), wired then probed in wiring.rs; supported schema version → 5. (d) `scrape github owner/repo` records the snapshot in one tx and prints the contributors block (no `[n] ` markers). (e) Narrow existing tests (acceptance-review #2).
criteria: CL-1: `scrape github BurntSushi/ripgrep` records 30 humans ranked by commits as links to github:BurntSushi/ripgrep, prints `Contributors recorded: 30` + `bots excluded` naming each bot, writes zero claims.
Migration v5 is forward-only and idempotent: opening a v4 store upgrades it; re-opening a v5 store is a no-op; the store reports schema version 5.
A store where the link adapter's probe fails (upsert-twice sentinel does not refresh rank or alters first-observed) refuses to start with a structured `health.startup.refused` event.
The contributors block carries no `[n] ` markers; the shipped scrape_github / scrape_sign / scrape_candidates / scrape_auth suites and viewer_is_read_only stay green (the viewer records no links).
`assert_no_claim_persisted` doc and the two `…persists_nothing…` test titles say `persists no claim`; their assertions are unchanged and green.
acceptance_criteria: CL-1: `scrape github BurntSushi/ripgrep` records 30 humans ranked by commits as links to github:BurntSushi/ripgrep, prints `Contributors recorded: 30` + `bots excluded` naming each bot, writes zero claims.

steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. Functional paradigm (ADR-007): selection is a total pure function over raw rows + N; effects (HTTP, DuckDB) stay in adapter-github / adapter-duckdb / the cli verb. PBT (test-scenarios.md §7 #1): output size = min(N, distinct humans); no bot-rule match; ranks contiguous 1..=k; permutation-invariant; de-dup by id. Adapter integration test on a REAL DuckDB file: record_snapshot never lowers the row set nor touches first_observed_at. Viewer: link recording lives in the cli scrape verb, not behind GithubPort — the viewer's wiring gets no ContributionLinkPort. If DELIVER instead shares a harvest function with the viewer, add `contribution_links` to the viewer_invariants universe in this step (acceptance-review #6). The WS stays RED after this step (no `infer` verb yet).
steps.estimated_effort: 8h (port ext + pure selection + v5 migration + link adapter/probe + scrape wiring)
steps.mutation_note: Bot rule, re-rank and top-N cut are the load-bearing pure branches; include scraper-domain people selection in per-feature mutation. Upsert must never touch first_observed_at (killed by the adapter integration test + probe).

steps.name: Walking skeleton GREEN: `infer people --sign 1` signs an evidence-backed adherence through the shared sign batch
steps.description: Thin thread of slices 02+03 over the 01-01 links, just enough for WS-CPI-1. PURE (scraper-domain people): eligibility (embodiesPhilosophy, relationship You|SubscribedPeer), group by (person, philosophy), integer-hundredths confidence (DDD-9), ADR-064 evidence encoding, deterministic numbering. SHELL: NEW `openlore infer people [--sign N[,N…]]` verb reading links via ContributionLinkPort and repo claims via StoragePort::query_federated_by_subject (DDD-6). SIGN: extract the scraper `--sign` batch into a shared verb-neutral helper; ComposedClaim gains `references` (default empty ⇒ every existing CID unchanged) (DDD-12).
criteria: WS-CPI-1: after two scrapes and two signed memory-safety repo claims, `infer people --sign 1` (confidence 0.45, publish declined) exits 0 and signs exactly one claim `github:BurntSushi adheresToPhilosophy memory-safety` by Maria at 0.45 with no references.
WS-CPI-1: the signed evidence is exactly [ripgrep claim AT-URI, ripgrep commits?author=BurntSushi URL, regex claim AT-URI, regex commits URL] (ADR-064 order).

WS is already un-ignored (RED: `unrecognized subcommand 'infer'`); no un-ignore needed. Keep each slice's piece THIN: no markers/retraction/supersede eligibility (02-02), no --person/--min-repos (02-03), no STRONGER (04-02). steps.name: `--contributors N` overrides the count within 0..=100, costs at most one extra public request, and is refused on a person target
steps.description: US-CPI-001 AC3 + KPI-CPI-5 + OD-CPI-7 + UC-1/UC-3. Add clap `--contributors N` to `scrape github` (bounded 0..=100; rejected on a user target with a message naming owner/repo targets — both BEFORE any GitHub request). N counts humans after the bot rule. N = 0 records none, says so, and makes no contributors request.

steps.name: Recorded people are ranked by commits whatever GitHub's order, overlap with other scraped repos is shown, and re-scrapes never lose anyone — enforced by check-arch
steps.description: US-CPI-001 AC2/AC4/AC5 + D-4 + DDD-16. Harden selection against the FakeGithub lie catalogue (out-of-order rows, `type: Bot`, `[bot]` login typed User, case variants, duplicate ids). Pure overlap: people linked to other scraped repos, rendered as `Also contributes to repos you scraped` lines (no `[n] ` markers). Re-scrape refreshes rank/commits/last-observed, never deletes, never touches first-observed. xtask check-arch gains `contribution_links_append_only` and the adapter-github port-reference guard.
criteria: CL-13: whatever order GitHub returns rows in, recorded people are humans ranked by commits desc then login asc, with bots (by type or case-insensitive `[bot]` suffix) excluded and duplicate ids recorded once.
CL-2: after scraping rust-lang/regex, scraping BurntSushi/ripgrep prints `BurntSushi → rust-lang/regex` under `Also contributes to repos you scraped`.
CL-5: a re-scrape where one earlier contributor dropped out keeps that link with its original last-observed date; other links show refreshed rank/commits; no first-observed value changes.

`xtask check-arch` fails on any DELETE/DROP/TRUNCATE/bare UPDATE against contribution_links in adapter-duckdb, and on adapter-github naming a storage or identity port; a synthetic violation unit test proves each rule fires.

steps.name: A failed contributor harvest records nothing and exits non-zero; a too-large or empty repo is a named notice with exit 0
steps.description: US-CPI-001 AC6 + DDD-14 + UC-2. adapter-github classifies /contributors outcomes: 403 rate-limit, 401 stale PAT, malformed rows (→ ApiShape), 403 'too large' and 204 empty (→ ContributorsUnavailable). The scrape aborts on the first three BEFORE any link write (no partial snapshot), naming the cause (GITHUB_TOKEN hint on rate limit; token never echoed); the latter two print `Contributors not recorded` + reason, record nothing, exit 0.
criteria: CL-6: a rate-limited /contributors read reports the rate limit, suggests GITHUB_TOKEN, records zero links, exits non-zero.
CL-7: a rejected token records zero links, exits non-zero, and the token never appears in stdout or stderr.
CL-8: a contributor list with a row missing login/id records zero links (no partial snapshot) and exits non-zero naming an unexpected response.
CL-9 + CL-10: a 'too large' 403 or an empty-repo 204 prints `Contributors not recorded` with `too large` / `empty`, records zero links, still shows the repo candidates, exits 0.
acceptance_criteria: CL-6: a rate-limited /contributors read reports the rate limit, suggests GITHUB_TOKEN, records zero links, exits non-zero.
CL-7: a rejected token records zero links, exits non-zero, and the token never appears in stdout or stderr.
CL-8: a contributor list with a row missing login/id records zero links (no partial snapshot) and exits non-zero naming an unexpected response.
CL-9 + CL-10: a 'too large' 403 or an empty-repo 204 prints `Contributors not recorded` with `too large` / `empty`, records zero links, still shows the repo candidates, exits 0.
steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. Reuse ADR-019 status classification + no-token-leak; distinguish the 'too large' 403 from the rate-limit 403 by GitHub's documented body/headers, pinned in the FakeGithub gold fixtures (DDD-15 lie catalogue — the recorded-fixture contract test for this external API). Atomicity is structural: the snapshot is written only from a complete in-memory selection in one transaction. After this step all 14 non-live contributor_links scenarios are active.
steps.mutation_note: Mutation must kill any branch that writes links on an error outcome or treats ContributorsUnavailable as fatal / rate-limit as a notice.

steps.name: Only active, non-retracted, non-superseded, non-marker repo claims support an inference — self-retraction rule hoisted into claim-domain
steps.description: DDD-7 + D-2 + UC-6.
